UNODC fully applies a gender perspective in the implementation of all activities under the project. Throughout the reporting period UNODC sought the nomination of a genderbalanced pools of participants in all its invitation letters 100 which led to the nomination of 56 female participants out 140 overall 40. Finally UNDOC provided access to selected practitioners to its online Training Module Gender Dimensions of Criminal Justice Responses to Terrorism.The goal is being met so far.

The events will utilize the UNODC Practical Guide and the newly developed TraintheTrainers Module on handling electronic evidence funded by the European Union. In 2023 UNODC began the process of designing and producing training videos tailored to the context of Maldives adapting existing scripts on international cooperation and data disclosure to reflect the current legal framework of the country including reference to the Evidence Act Act No. 112022 where possible. During the reporting period the video scripts were translated into Dhivehi a recording company was hired and the recorded audio that will be overlayed in the videos was delivered to UNODC. The roundtable will include a TableTop exercise using the newly developed Model Request Forms to request electronic evidence. In the reporting period UNODC began preparing for the implementation of Activity 2.1.3 on the delivery of a crossregional legislative round table. Previously scheduled to take place in December 2023 due to difficulties in securing a suitable venue during the high season for tourism in Maldives the event has been postponed to now take place from 25 to 27 February 2024.

comment.narrative: Activities to be implemented within Output 2.2 will include the provision of advisory support through one mission and consultation with national stakeholders on evidencerelated matters.

IN PROGRESSWhen originally developed advisory consultations under Activity 2.2.1 were intended to involve a review of the national laws and procedures relating to evidence in criminal proceedings in Maldives as well as those governing related MLA including specific legislation rules and regulations. However due to the lengthy review negotiation and approval process required in the agreement of the project by the time implementation commenced steps had already been taken at national level to amend existing legislation covering evidence and MLA with numerous bills now submitted to the Peoples Majlis for review. As such the project team discussed possibilities for reformulating the activity while still safeguarding achievement of the relevant project output. It was decided that the most appropriate course of action was to organize an initial advisory consultation with key stakeholders to ascertain what support is required in the implementation of newly amended and soon to be enacted legislation thereby ensuring respect for all relevant international standards is maintained.On 1 June 2023 UNODC met with representatives of the Bar Council the Department of Judicial Administration and the PGO to initiate these discussions. Through the consultations national stakeholders confirmed that traininginformation materials have been prepared on several topics related to the forthcoming legislation and the previous laws it is amending such as leaflets for witnesseslay people on what to expect before coming to court. It was explained that while help may not be required in the development of these training materials themselves there is a potential need for similar products related to the Evidence Act Act No. 112022 and a definite need for existing and possibly future materials to be converted into training videos for digestibility and ease of circulation. UNODC confirmed that these requests could certainly be considered in the context of the project and confirmed that the best course of action would be for the national stakeholders to collate a list of technical assistance priorities in the areas discussed for submission to UNODC following which a collective decision will be made on suitable next steps. UNODC is still awaiting communication of these technical assistance priorities but is ready to respond as soon as they are shared.

IN PROGRESSActivity 2.4.1 Develop and deliver basic and specialized training programmes for prosecutors to enhance their capabilities on the prosecution of terrorismrelated cases occurred at sea. UNODC delivered training workshops for 15 judges from 22 to 24 August 2023 and for 15 prosecutors from 4 to 6 September 2023 to enhance their capacities in dealing with maritimerelated terrorism cases. The workshops focused on the application of Maldives national law in line with the provisions of UNCLOS and UNTOC. In addition UNODC plans to conduct a training workshop from 19 to 21 February 2024 for eight prosecutors and seven judges to equip them with the necessary tools and best international practices to combat violent extremism and terrorism at sea which will entail providing practitioners with knowledge about international treaties and underscoring their crucial link to the prevention and countering of terrorism. Activity 2.4.2 Conduct regular multiagency workshops with law enforcement and prosecution actors to discuss challenges and recommendations on the prosecution of maritime terrorism cases. UNODC recognizing the need to bridge the gap between maritime law enforcement officials particularly Coast Guard boarding officers and police investigators and criminal justice actors particularly prosecutors and judges plans to conduct a training workshop seeking to provide relevant knowledge on boarding procedures investigation package preparation prosecution tactics and best practices on adjudication of terrorism cases at sea. The workshop scheduled to take place from 4 to 6 March 2024 will seek to familiarize four Coast Guard officers five police investigators and six prosecutors with the application of such practices within the Maldivian criminal justice system in line with domestic and international legislation.Activity 2.4.3 Conduct a study trip abroad for legal actors to improve their exposure to other jurisdictions on the prosecution of maritime terrorism cases. UNODC plans to conduct a study tour to Washington D.C. to provide the opportunity to one prosecutor one judge one police officer and one magistrate to improve exposure to the jurisdiction of the United States of America and their considerable experience in terrorism cases. The participants will visit State courts federal court prosecutors offices the Department of Justice the Marshalls Office the Organized Crime Unit of the Prosecutors Office and the Bureau of Counterterrorism. The study tour is planned to take place in May 2024 for a period of one week.Activity 2.4.4 Translate legislation policies manuals regulations andor training materials fromto EnglishDhivehi to facilitate engagements of international experts and local beneficiaries. UNODC has translated 28 key maritime and terrorismrelated laws and regulations including those related to various maritime zones fisheries acts and prison regulations. In addition UNODC is currently translating the mandates of the key agencies in Maldives whose mandate may be linked to the countering of terrorism at sea. All these translations will help UNODC staff and consultants to better understand the local legislative framework identify existing legal gaps prepare for trainings and workshops and identify solutions to fill legal gaps through the application of international instruments.

comment.narrative: Activities to be implemented within Output 3.1 will include 1 conducting an assessment of existing maritime policing practices to identify capacitybuilding opportunities of Marine Police Department and its officers 2 provide technical advice to Maldives Police Service to harmonize mandates and roles among units and departments for the prevention and countering of maritime terrorism 3 based on the assessment conducted develop and deliver associated training programmes to strengthen the capabilities of Marine Police Department officers such as vessel boarding navigational training andor antiterrorism at sea 4 identify and procure specialized equipment to improve Marine Police Departments capabilities for maritime policing to prevent and disrupt terrorist incidents in Maldives internal waters and territorial sea.

IMPLEMENTEDActivity 3.1.2 Provide technical advice to Maldives Police Service to harmonize mandates and roles among units and departments for the prevention and countering of maritime terrorism.IN PROGRESSActivity 3.1.1 Strengthened maritime policing strategy to ensure safety of the Maldives territorial waters to disrupt terrorism threats. UNODC conducted onetoone meetings with the Defence Intelligence Services DIS the Coast Guard the Head of Information Analysis in NCTC Maldives Immigration the Maldives Monetary Authoritys Financial Intelligence Unit FIU the Head of Homeland Security Police Services and Maldives Customs Services in July 2023 to convince relevant stakeholders to hold an interagency dialogue and promote communication on intelligencesharing threat assessments and informationsharing. The assessment will continue with dedicated meetings in April and May 2024.Activity 3.1.3 Based on the assessment conducted develop and deliver associated training programmes to strengthen the capabilities of Marine Police Department officers such as vessel boarding navigational training andor antiterrorism at sea. In parallel with and building on activities focused on enhancing maritime law enforcement capabilities in detecting waterborne IEDs Output 3.2 UNODC delivered two courses respectively focusing on countering waterborne IEDs CWBIED and on countering chemical biological radiological and nuclear explosives CBRNE. These courses sought to improve interagency response and coordination mechanisms visvis maritime terrorist incidents. The courses in particular aimed at enhancing the knowledge and informationsharing capacity of the Maldives Marine Police as well as the MNDF Explosive Ordinance Division and Coast Guard to improve information sharing in preventing and responding to the use of WBIED and CBRNE for terrorist purposes. The CWBIED training was held from 16 to 27 July 2023 for twenty MNDF Coast Guard officials and four Maldives Forensic Police Officers. The course on CBRNE took place from 30 July to 10 August 2023 and gathered eight Coast Guard eight MPS four Maldives Ports Officers and four Maldives Customs Officers. UNODC is also planning tabletop exercises TTXs for delivery in May 2024 on maritime policing to provide core guidance to the Marine Police Department in performing marine operations in the territorial waters while considering legal mandates operational capabilities and resource constraints. Further training for the police is scheduled for May 2024.Activity 3.1.4 Identify and procure specialized equipment to improve MPDs capabilities for maritime policing to prevent and disrupt terrorist incidents in Maldives internal waters and territorial sea. Based on the requirement and proposal received from Marine Police Department UNODC has procured 16 boarding vests and 20 engine spare parts to the vessels of Marine Police Department. In addition the procurement of a drone and monitors for the Marine Police is currently ongoing.

comment.narrative: Activities to be implemented within Output 3.2 will include 1 establish a working group specialized on countering waterborne improvised explosive devices WBIED for the exchange of knowledge and practices among maritime law enforcement agencies 2 provide technical advice to maritime law enforcement agencies on improving the WBIED prevention and response mechanisms 3 identify and procure specialized equipment for the detection of WBIED.

IN PROGRESSActivity 3.2.1 Establish a working group specialized on countering waterborne improvised explosive devices CWBIED for the exchange of knowledge and practices among maritime law enforcement agencies. UNODC conducted several onetoone meetings with MNDF MPS NCTC Maldives Ports Limited Maldives Customs Maldives Aviation Services and the Monetary Authority in November 2023 and presented the intention of establishing a working group specialized in CWBIED to sustain existing and ongoing collaboration and facilitate recurrent meetings among maritime law enforcement agencies for the exchange of knowledge and practices among maritime law enforcement agencies. Based on the feedback from the agencies UNODC has developed a terms of reference ToR to establish a working group and foster a culture of cooperation and coordination to effectively address the evolving threats related to WBIEDs to improve communication and coordination among agencies involved in countering WBIEDs and to advocate for the necessary resources and legislation to effectively address the threat of WBIEDs. UNODC is planning to present the ToR at the first working group establishment meeting in February 2024 and thereafter to conduct two supportive followup meetings to incorporate the inputs of the relevant agencies and to support the first working group meeting.Activity 3.2.2 Provide technical advice to maritime law enforcement agencies on improving the WBIED prevention and response mechanisms. UNODC conducted a two week WBIED training from 19 to 30 November 2023 for six students of the MNDF Coast Guard six students of the MNDFs Explosive Ordnance Disposal unit EOD three students of MPS and two students of the MNDF Marines on Safe Working Practices Boarding Procedures Tactical Concepts Procedures IED Definitions and Types IED Potential Indicators Placements and Vulnerable Points Countering IEDs actions on IEDs and producing METHANE M Major incident declared E Exact location. T Type of incident. H Hazards present or suspected. A Access routes that are safe to use report exercises Crime Scene Investigation and Evidence collection. The training also included practical elements to cement the knowledge of officers and practice the process of gathering evidence correctly and team configurationrole assignments. During the scenarios officers conducted risk assessments before undertaking boarding evolutions in a safe manner. Scenarios were introduced with inert IEDs and components and the team tasked with uncovering the items and react accordingly and safely.Activity 3.2.3 Identify and procure specialized equipment for the detection of WBIED. Based on the proposal received from the MNDF UNODC has initiated the procurement of four telescopic search mirrors one underwater metal detector one explosive ordinance disposal tool kit five gas detectors one underwater communication system and one remotely operated vehicle ROV to conduct efficient search operations detect and positively identify WBIEDs and to facilitate communication between EOD divers and surface offices.

IMPLEMENTEDActivity 3.4.1 Provide training andor onsite mentoring to law enforcement agencies on the adoption of best international practices to gather and process information conducive to the detection of terrorist threats at sea.Activity 3.4.3 Develop and deliver maritime intelligence training programmes to law enforcement officers outside of the Greater Male Region to improve counterterrorism capabilities in remote locationsIN PROGRESSActivity 3.4.4 Identify and procure equipment andor analysis software to strengthen maritime intelligence capabilities of law enforcement agencies to disrupt terrorism at sea. UNODC provided the Coast Guard with access to Marine Traffic Global Satellite webbased platform to access the most recent positions of vessels received by satellite and to get the most uptodate vessel location information and to follow the vessels of interest. In the same vein UNODC has started the procurement for underwater and nightvision cameras an unmanned aerial vehicle and longrange night vision binoculars for Marine Police. Such equipment will assist officers to overcome challenges related to underwater sea operations and nighttime patrolling. UNODC is also currently running a procurement to equip MNDF with GETAC A140 ruggedized tablets with advanced analytical software tailored for maritime intelligence for the realtime analysis of data and access to critical information.NOT IMPLEMENTEDActivity 3.4.2 Provide technical advice to maritime law enforcement agencies towards establishing an effective information sharing mechanism to improve communication and coordination on preventing and countering terrorism. The activities will be implemented once the Information Fusion Centre is established in Mal.

comment.narrative: Activities to be implemented under Output 4.1 will include 1 support Maldives Correctional Service MCS to develop a stronger rehabilitation framework that is applied in all prisons in the country with equal and equitable access to all prisoners targeted interventions for VEP women prisoners and overrepresented groups such as people with substance use disorders who are vulnerable to radicalization efforts 2 support MCS in establishing partnership with public and private sector as well as NGOs and community leaders to ensure sustainable implementation of rehabilitation interventions and linkages with community service providers for a wholeofsociety approach to preventing violent extremism and radicalization 3 support MCS to develop rehabilitation programs build vocation skills to engage prisoners during their period of incarceration and prepare them for a life outside prison.

IMPLEMENTEDActivity 4.1.1 Support the MCS to develop a stronger rehabilitation framework that is applied in all prisons in the country with equal and equitable access to all prisoners targeted interventions for VEPs women prisoners and overrepresented groups such as people with substance use disorders who are vulnerable to radicalization efforts.IN PROGRESSActivity 4.1.3 Support the MCS to develop rehabilitation programs build vocation skills to engage prisoners during their period of incarceration and prepare them for a life outside prison. IN PROGRESSActivity 4.4.1 Legislative and policy guidance and advisory support to ensure legislative policy and operations procedures are equally and similarly applied across all prisons under the MCS jurisdiction within considerations of gender and age specific needs. At the request of the MCS UNODC provided technical assistance necessary to develop a fiveyear prison reform strategy that encapsulates legislative policy and operational revisions required to strengthen the Service. UNODC recruited an international Prison Expert who conducted an initial assessment in country and produced a draft strategy document with recommendations. The draft document was informed by individual assessments and feedback from relevant experts on ground in the areas of RR violent extremist prisoners VEP Management and application of human rights standards in detention. In addition feedback received through multiple consultations with other stakeholders in Maldives PGO MPS Huma Rights Commission of Maldives National Integrity Commission NIC British and American projects with MCS in house experts of UNODC and MCS was also incorporated. A twoday validation workshop with the participation of 22 senior officials of MCS was organized to finalize the input for the MCS strategy in December 2023. In delivering the activity UNODC sought synergies with the British High Commission and the consultants hired under a parallel initiative to ensure coordination and potential engagements with MCS under RR. The draft strategy is currently under review.

comment.narrative: Activities to be delivered under Output 4.5 will include 1 provide technical advice to senior prison management staff on the best use and practices of a prisoner data management system PDMS to facilitate reporting enable the development of targeted rehabilitation programmes and improve overall resource planning 2 conduct trainings sessions on the use of Maldives Correctional Services PDMS to relevant prison officers across prison establishments.

IN PROGRESS Activity 4.5.1 Provide technical advice to senior prison management staff on the best use and practices of a PDMS to facilitate reporting enable the development of targeted rehabilitation programmes and improve overall resource planning. During the project inception MCS informed UNODC of their wishes to introduce a new digitized Offender Management System OMS and IT infrastructure for which a governmentinitiated procurement process was ongoing. In this context UNODC offered technical assistance to design the new OMS following government identification of a suitable vendor. However towards the fourth quarter 2023 MCS informed UNODC that the bidding process was stalled. During the validation workshop held in December 2023 UNODC reiterated the recommendation to introduce an OMS at MCS to facilitate record maintenance resource planning case management and sentence planning in a more efficient manner. UNODC suggested incorporating already shared concepts of RR following Risk Need Responsivity Model into the design of the same which was endorsed by MCS. Following discussions with MCS Senior Management and IT specialists UNODC facilitated a demonstration of the HORUS 360 iOMS its individual thematic modules and workflow processes in order to inspire and create a basic yet practical system. Despite its complexity the demonstration provided MCS with a greater understanding and clarity of its requirements as well as the potential designs that can be adopted. Building on the above UNODC intends facilitate a presentation of the OMS introduced by Ghana Prisons to further increase awareness on the requirements and potential avenues to support the establishment of a contextualised yet intelligent OMS for MCS in 2024. NOT IMPLEMENTEDActivity 4.5.2 Conduct training sessions on the use of the Maldives Correctional Services PDMS to relevant prison officers across prison establishments. The training sessions on the use is dependent on the design and adoption of an OMS by MCS.
